title: VPC mirrored artifact allowlist and staged-patch upgrade contract (private deploy)
creator: Aisha Grant
description: This ticket defines requirements and acceptance criteria for enabling Private/VPC customers to run Redwood Private with a locked-down egress posture using mirrored artifact registries and an allowlist-first upgrade process. Scope covers: registry mirror configuration (OCI/Docker blobs), minimal runtime egress (timeboxed bootstrap), image signing verification, staged patch rollouts (canary -> ramp -> full), automated rollback triggers, and runbook/observability required for handoff to SOC/ops teams. Excludes: implementation-level build pipeline for image production; that is covered in ENG backlog. The goal is a contract that lets Sales/CS promise a predictable upgrade path for regulated customers while preserving zero-surprise offline upgrades and repairability.
acceptance_criteria: Artifact mirroring: Customers can configure a single inbound-initiated mirror (pull) or push-based sync to an on-prem/private registry. Mirror configuration docs and sample scripts must be provided.

Allowlist-first egress: By default, runtime nodes must not perform DNS or outbound HTTPS calls except to allowlisted endpoints (artifact mirror, license/KMS endpoints, optional monitoring proxy). An explicit minimal egress matrix (hostnames, IP ranges, ports, protocols) must be published and validated in integration tests.

Timeboxed bootstrap egress: Where unavoidable (e.g., initial image/content bootstrap), system must support a time-limited egress window with automatic closure after artifact sync completes. The console must show bootstrap status and elapsed window.

Image provenance: All images/artifacts consumed by the cluster must be signed (sigstore/cosign or equivalent). Upgrade agent verifies signatures against customer-provided root(s) and refuses unsigned images. Verification errors surface as upgrade-blocking events.

Staged rollout policy: Product provides a default staged-patch policy (canary 5% for 30 minutes -> ramp 25% for 1 hour -> full) configurable by operator. Rollouts must support pause and rollback steps triggered manually or automatically on health signals.

Rollback criteria: Automatic rollback should trigger if any of the following happen during rollout: 1) 50% increase in 5xx errors vs baseline, 2) 30% regression in p95 latency vs baseline, 3) <95% success rate on startup readiness probes across canary pool for 15 minutes.

Health & observability: Console exposes per-rollout metrics (success rate, p50/p95 latency, error rate, token/throughput impact), a rollout timeline, and a single-click abort/rollback button. Alerts for failed rollouts are wired to customer alerting endpoints.

Offline validation: A test harness must run pre-upgrade smoke checks that operate without outbound egress (using mirrored artifacts only). The harness reports artifact checksum matches, signature verification, and container start confirmations.
Upgrade artifact lifecycle: Artifact retention, purge, and re-provisioning policies are documented. The upgrade agent supports resume after partial sync and verifies checksums before applying images.

Runbook: An ops runbook with step-by-step instructions for controlled upgrade, emergency rollback, re-mirroring artifacts, and house-keeping tasks (mirror re-seed, key rotation) is published and reviewed by Security and SRE.

Compliance & auditing: All upgrade events (who/what/when/checksums) are written to auditable logs and available via the customer's audit log pipeline. Audit entries include signed metadata for chain-of-custody.

Test matrix: Acceptance tests cover three network modes: full-online (no egress restrictions), allowlist-only (mirrors + KMS endpoints), and fully air-gapped (artifact import via USB/mirror import). Each mode has a pass/fail checklist automated in CI or documented manual steps.
